request:
Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Should anyone be able to see the whole board, or only the desk staff? And should the desk be the only people who can mark items as claimed, or can anyone do it?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Do you want any proof of ownership checked before an item is marked claimed, or does the desk just type in the owner's name and the date they collected it?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should items that nobody claims be removed or hidden after some time, or should they stay on the board forever?
A: No preference: you decide.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).

from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app import app

c = TestClient(app)
B = {"description": "Blue umbrella", "location": "Library", "date_found": "2024-05-01"}


def test_flow():
    r = c.post("/items", json=B)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    i = r.json()
    assert i["claimed"] is False and i["owner_name"] is None
    other = c.post("/items", json=B).json()
    assert c.get(f"/items/{i['id']}").json()["location"] == "Library"
    assert c.get("/items/999999").status_code == 404
    assert len(c.get("/items").json()) >= 2
    r = c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/claim", json={"owner_name": "Ann"})
    assert r.status_code == 200 and r.json()["claimed"] and r.json()["owner_name"] == "Ann"
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/claim", json={"owner_name": "Bob"}).status_code == 409
    assert c.get(f"/items/{i['id']}").json()["owner_name"] == "Ann"
    ids = [x["id"] for x in c.get("/items?claimed=false").json()]
    assert other["id"] in ids and i["id"] not in ids
    assert c.post("/items/999999/claim", json={"owner_name": "x"}).status_code == 404


def test_validation():
    assert c.post("/items", json={"description": "x"}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post("/items", json={**B, "date_found": "nope"}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post("/items", json={**B, "description": " "}).status_code == 422
    i = c.post("/items", json=B).json()
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/claim", json={}).status_code == 422
    assert c.post(f"/items/{i['id']}/claim", json={"owner_name": ""}).status_code == 422

text:
I wrote `app.py` and `tests/test_app.py`, and both tests pass.

- `POST /items` reports a found item. It needs `description`, `location` and `date_found` (YYYY-MM-DD), and blank values are rejected. It returns 201 with the new item.
- `GET /items` lists everything on the board. Adding `?claimed=false` shows only the items still waiting for their owners.
- `GET /items/{id}` shows one item, or 404 if it doesn't exist.
- `POST /items/{id}/claim` takes `{"owner_name": "..."}` and marks the item as claimed with that name. It returns 404 if the item doesn't exist and 409 if the item was already claimed. A blank or missing name is rejected with a 422.

You left these choices open, so I kept it simple. There are no logins, so anyone can view the board and mark an item claimed. There is no proof-of-ownership check, and unclaimed items stay on the board indefinitely. Data is stored in `lostfound.db` in the project folder.
